title: Agroforestry adoption at scale
bottleneck: Integrating trees into farmland improves soil, sequesters carbon, diversifies income, and buffers climate shocks — yet adoption is low because trees take years to pay off, complicate mechanization, and tenure insecurity discourages long-term investment. The benefits are diffuse and long-term; the costs are immediate and concrete. Extension systems built for annual crops don't know how to support tree-crop systems. Extension systems built for annual crops do not know how to support tree-crop systems.
why_it_blocks: Agroforestry is one of the few practices that simultaneously addresses soil, climate, and income. Its failure to scale leaves all three problems worse.
current_state: FAO promotes agroforestry among its proven solutions; adoption lags, cited as low in most regional assessments. FAO promotes agroforestry among its proven solutions, yet adoption lags in most regional assessments.
